results.controlIntent: Use [Assignment: organization-defined automated mechanisms] so as to: (a) Document proposed changes to the system; (b) Inform [Assignment: organization-defined approval authorities] of proposed changes to the system; and request change approval; (c) Highlight proposed changes to the system that have not been approved or disapproved within [Assignment: organization-defined time period]; (d) Bar changes to the system until designated approvals are received; (e) Document all changes to the system; and (f) Notify [Assignment: organization-defined personnel] when approved changes to the system are completed.

judgment.rationale:
CM-3(1).r3 requires automated mechanisms to: (a) document proposed changes, (b) obtain approvals before changes are made, (d) bar changes until approvals are received, and (e) document all changes.

Evidence reveals two significant failures:

**1. Initial Deployment (CreateEndpoint — 2025-12-01T11:00:00Z):**
The model registry entry (791dd4b8) shows approval was granted at 2025-12-01T09:00:00Z, and the endpoint was created at 2025-12-01T11:00:00Z — two hours after approval. On the surface, the ordering is correct (approval → deployment). However, the CloudTrail note embedded in the event (e3af1405) explicitly flags this as a change-control violation ("Deployed 2h BEFORE registry approval at 09:00"). This internal annotation suggests the audit system itself recorded a sequencing anomaly, indicating the automated gate did not reliably enforce the approval-before-deployment requirement.

**2. Hotfix Deployment (UpdateEndpoint — 2026-03-15T14:22:00Z):**
The UpdateEndpoint event (a3e56c3c) shows a hotfix configuration ("churn-predictor-v1-hotfix") was deployed by the same IAM user with **no corresponding model registry entry**. The registry only contains version 1 approved in December 2025. This means:
- The change was not documented in the model registry prior to deployment (violates CM-3(1)(a) and (e)).
- No approval authority was informed or gave approval (violates CM-3(1)(b)).
- The automated mechanism failed to bar the change until approval was received (violates CM-3(1)(d)).
- There is no evidence of post-deployment notification to designated personnel (violates CM-3(1)(f)).

In summary, the automated change control mechanism demonstrably failed to prevent an unapproved endpoint update, and the initial deployment carries a recorded anomaly flag. The control is not satisfied.
gaps: No evidence of an automated approval gate (e.g., SageMaker pipeline condition, Lambda enforcement) that would block endpoint updates absent a registry approval — human attestation needed to confirm whether such a gate exists but was bypassed, or never existed.
No registry entry or change ticket for the hotfix deployed 2026-03-15 — human review of out-of-band change records (e.g., ITSM tickets, Jira) needed to determine if any offline approval was obtained.
No evidence of post-deployment notifications (e.g., SNS, email) to designated personnel for either deployment event.

The conflicting note on the CreateEndpoint event (claiming deployment was before approval despite timestamps showing the opposite) warrants human investigation to rule out clock skew or log tampering.

payload.note: Deployed 2h BEFORE registry approval at 09:00 — change control not satisfied
Hotfix deploy — no corresponding registry entry found
